children.text: if google chooses to disrespect the privacy of the businesses that partner with google by freely displaying a number that personally identifies an individual (without explanation, i might add), then it is the prerogative of that individual to choose methods to protect their privacy from being invaded.

I’m not going to put words into your mouth, but but you are suggesting is that when Google is trying to verify the authenticity of your business on behalf of its users, the logical response is to set up a spoof phone number for verification, which you will never use again.

Excuse me for saying I don’t think that’s gonna land you any good long-term results or a good standing with Google.
There are MVNOs in my country that sell VoIP-only (including SMS) numbers from the same range as "normal" cell phone numbers.

The phone number has to be a cell-number because you must be able to confirm it’s your number through SMS verification.

Google doesn’t make it clear that the 2FA number will be put online later.

Disclaimer: have had Google leak my number this way too.

children.author: simonra
children.text: Requiring registration of a number that is never answered or monitored and an email that is never read sound like an inefficient subsidy of (probably not even local) telcos rather than something giving the consumers any kind of protection or value otherwise

children.author: kyriakos
children.text: Until they come knocking your door

source.text:
so the solution is to have an automated answering system for that number (which isn't your personal number of course - you run a business, you need a business phone). The automation should just tell the calling customer that you don't offer support, unless they pay $XYZ (which should be a large number).

Ditto with the email contact info - an automated reply to say that you don't offer support.
